posts.title: Welcome to My Blog
posts.summary: A quick intro to why I'm starting to write and what you can expect here.
posts.content:
Hey! I'm Christopher, and this is the first post on my new blog section. I've wanted a place to write about what I'm working on, things I'm learning, and general updates about my journey as a software engineer — so here it is.

Expect posts about projects I'm building, interesting problems I've run into, things I'm learning in my CS courses at UF, and occasionally just life stuff. Thanks for stopping by!

posts.title: Building a RAG Chatbot for an Online Course
posts.summary: A behind-the-scenes look at building an AI-powered course assistant using LangChain and FAISS.
posts.content:
One of my current projects is an AI chatbot embedded into a Thinkific-based leadership training course. The idea is simple: learners can ask the chatbot questions, and it responds using the actual course material rather than just hallucinating answers.

The core of it is a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline. I process all the course PDFs and text into vector embeddings using LangChain, store them in a FAISS index, and then at query time I retrieve the most relevant chunks and pass them to an LLM as context.

The trickiest part so far has been chunking strategy — too small and you lose context, too large and you waste the context window. I ended up with overlapping chunks of ~500 tokens which seems to strike a good balance.

The frontend is a lightweight chat widget built in plain HTML/CSS/JS that floats over the course content. More updates to come as this progresses!
